subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and if so should the public contract be global, per-agent, hostname-scoped, or folded into a broader egress policy?
rationale: The source shows the primitive exists, but the requested config widens an SSRF boundary and creates a public config contract; automation should not choose metadata, redirect, cache, provider, audit, and authorization semantics without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve Nested SSRF Policy
options.body: Land a narrowly documented default-off `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` design that composes with the existing fake-IP flags and includes explicit security semantics before implementation.

options.title: Keep Current Narrow Support
options.body: Leave current main as-is and document that arbitrary private-network `web_fetch` remains intentionally unsupported while fake-IP proxy ranges stay the only scoped opt-ins.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Egress Design
options.body: Route this through the broader egress firewall or confirmation work so private-network access, allowlists, and per-agent authorization are designed together.

recommendation.title: Approve Nested SSRF Policy
recommendation.body: Land a narrowly documented default-off `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` design that composes with the existing fake-IP flags and includes explicit security semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has both the maintainer discussion signal and the strongest recent SSRF/guarded-fetch history for the affected trust boundary.
